_meta.howToMerge: For each entry: if matchesCollection is set, merge over the journey gyuj-<id> (dates, departure, ordered stops, return, companions, summary, sources); the entries listed in alsoMatchesCollections are index entries subsumed by the same trip and should be shown as part of it (or linked to it), not as separate trips. Entries with matchesCollection null are new journeys with id cur-YYYY-MM-nn. A stop with confidence 'inferred' or a departure/return with evidence 'inferred' is a curator's inference from the cited text and must be labelled as such in the UI; 'documented' means the cited source states it. placeId is the gazetteer id (data/gazetteer.json, same scheme as parse-gyuj-collections.mjs); null placeId with placeIdNote means the locality is outside the gazetteer (non-Romanian) or not yet in it.
_meta.note: Only what a cited source states is recorded; inferences are marked. Where sources disagree (index vs chronology vs RFM melody data) the entry keeps both and says so in the note or summary. Dates in Bartok's letters and in the chronology are Gregorian.

journeys.summary: Bartok spent the summer and autumn of 1904 at Gerlice puszta in Gomor county as the guest of the Fischer family, working on the Rhapsody op. 1. There he heard a Fischer employee, Lidi Dosa from Kibed in Maros-Torda county, sing and notated one of her songs; the chronology dates the beginning of his folk-song collecting from this. The index entry 'Gerlicepuszta / Kibed' therefore combines the place of notation with the singer's home village.

journeys.summary: Bartok's systematic Romanian collecting began on 17 July 1909, when he travelled from Veszto via Nagyvarad to Belenyes, where Ioan Busitia had prepared the ground; he returned repeatedly to Belenyes as his base and worked in the villages of the upper Fekete-Koros valley. Villages with July-dated songs are Belenyes, Gyalany, Lehecseny, Hatar, Biharmezo and Telek; August-dated are Lelesd, Bondoraszo, Kereszely, Biharkristyor, Draganfalva, Belenyesszentmarton, Korossebes and Vaskohszeleste, plus Lehecseny and Biharmezo again. Around 7 August he fell ill in the heat and went to his sister at Szilad puszta; by his own count the summer yielded 320 Romanian songs (Kelemen: he arrived 17 July and started work the next day; the trip lasted over two weeks). The order of the village visits is not documented.

journeys.summary: Bartok used the Christmas holiday of 1910 for a trip among the Moti of the Aranyos valley: he arrived in Transylvania on 24 December, lodged at Abrudbanya from the 25th to the 28th, collected 45 songs at Kerpenyes on the 27th, moved his base to Topanfalva on the 28th and wrote from Fehervolgy on the 29th and 31st, where he was counted in the census. The villages of the trip are Feketevolgy, Kozepvidra, Fehervolgy, Bisztra, Also- and Felsovidra in Torda-Aranyos county; his wife sent fresh cylinders to Topanfalva on 2 and 3 January 1911, and on 4 January he set off along the Aranyos towards Torda. Kelemen adds that some villages of neighbouring Also-Feher county (Fenes, Ompolykovesd, dated January 1911 in RFM) were visited on the same trip. journeys.summary: The Torontal collecting of 1912 is documented in two phases. The chronology has Bartok leave for Valkany on 6 December, collect at Sarafalva on the 11th and break off; the melody data in RFM IV and Kelemen date the Valkany, Sarafalva and Egres material to November 1912, and Suchoff speaks of 'Torontal County material collected in November and December of 1912'. From about 16 December he worked outward from Temesvar: Keviszollos (22nd), Szephely (22-23 and 26), Gilad (23-24), then via Versec to Alibunar (27-28) and Petre (29), with further songs from Denta, Tolvad, Banlak and Ujozora; about 200 songs in all. With his cylinders used up he returned on 31 December, reaching Budapest on 1 January 1913.

journeys.summary: Bartok's preface to the Maramures volume states that he assembled its material from 15 to 27 March 1913 in eleven villages of Maramaros county - Ieud, Viseu de Jos, Bocicoel, Dragomiresti, Cuhea, Petrova, Poienile Izei, Glod, Valeni, Nanesti and Oncesti - travelling everywhere with the priest Ion Birlea of Ieud. journeys.summary: Freed from the Maramures manuscript, Bartok used the Christmas holiday of 1913 for a new area, Hunyad county. Between 21 and 28 December he made 82 recordings; on the 26th he collected at Paucsinesd (105 melodies within 24 hours according to Kelemen) and on the 28th wrote from Varhely that he had reached his 110th cylinder. The villages of the trip are Lelesz, Ohabasibisel, Nuksora, Paucsinesd, Malomviz, Feresd, Gyalar, Varhely and Cserbel (Kelemen adds Szocsed); he returned home on 4 January 1914. The material became the subject of his lecture and article 'A hunyadi roman nep zenedialektusa' (March 1914).
journeys.title: Hunyad county (Hateg region and the Poiana Rusca hills), December 21, 1913 - January 4, 1914

journeys.summary: On 3 April 1914 Bartok and his wife travelled to Marosvasarhely and from there collected on separate routes. His own itinerary is documented day by day: Disznajo (4-5 April), Marosliget and Marosvecs (6), Felsorepa (7), then Idecspataka, Libanfalva and Gorgenyhodak, Gorgenyorsova and Kincses (9), Nyaradremete from the evening of the 11th over Easter, Nyaradkoszvenyes (14), Jobbagytelke (15), the Gorgenyorsova-Kincsesfo-Felsooroszi-Nyaradremete round on the 16th, Bala (17) and Kortekapu (18). Marta Ziegler collected at Nyaradto, Marosliget, Mezoszabad and, according to Kelemen, Bala, Kortekapu, Maroskisfalud and Mezomajos (RFM marks her items 'Z.'). They left on 20 April and reached home at dawn on the 21st; the index splits the trip into four entries (87-90).

stops.note: Guest of Baron Adolf Kohner; collects from the estate staff and from Slovak harvest workers; one song from Kisules (Bars county) probably notated here. 195 records online.

journeys.summary: On 15 August 1918 Bartok left for what the chronology calls his last folk-song collecting trip in Hungary, to Felsoszaszberek puszta near Besenyszog as guest of Baron Adolf Kohner; he collected with good results from the estate staff and Slovak harvesters and finished on 26 August, returning via Ujszasz. In September he harmonised seven songs of the summer, among them Roza Okros's 'Angoli Borbala'.
journeys.title: Felsoszaszberek puszta (Besenyszog, Jasz-Nagykun-Szolnok county), August 15-26, 1918: last collecting trip in Hungary
